questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Mia sees many worms on the school path after every rainy day. She asks a question to test. Which prediction fits her pattern?
choices: There will be fewer worms after the next big rain.
There will be more worms after the next big rain.
There will be more worms on a hot, dry day.
There will be no worms on any path.
questions.explanation: Mia saw worms after rain each time. So she predicts the pattern will happen again after the next rain.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Tom tests which paper towel soaks up the most water. He uses three brands. What must he keep the same to make it a fair test?
choices: The brand of paper towel
The amount of water poured on each one
How much water each one soaks up
The colour of the pen he writes with
questions.explanation: Only the brand should change. The amount of water must stay the same, or the test is not fair.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A class votes for a favourite fruit. Apple got 6 votes, banana got 9 votes and mango got 4 votes. In a column graph, which column is the tallest?
choices: Apple
Mango
They are all the same
Banana
questions.explanation: Banana has the most votes, 9. The column with the most votes is the tallest.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Jack finds that paper plane A flies further than plane B. Lena tests the same planes and finds the opposite. What should they do first?
choices: Decide Jack is right because he went first
Compare how each of them ran the test
Throw away both planes
Pick the plane with the nicest colour
questions.explanation: Different results may mean the tests were not the same or not fair. Comparing how they tested helps them find out.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: For over 100 years, people in Australia have written down the daily temperature at weather stations. How does this data help scientists?
choices: It shows how temperatures have changed over time.
It makes the weather colder.
It tells them what colour the sky will be.
It is only useful for one day.
questions.explanation: Many records over many years let scientists see patterns and changes. They use this data to build explanations.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Scientists found that ultraviolet rays from the sun can damage skin. How has this explanation helped people in Australia?
choices: People now stay inside all year.
People now use hats, shade and sunscreen to stay safe.
People now have less summer.
People now wear dark glasses at night.
questions.explanation: Knowing why sunburn happens helps people fix the problem. Hats, shade and sunscreen protect skin from ultraviolet rays.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Scientists use measurements and observations to help build their explanations.
questions.explanation: Scientists collect data by measuring and observing. They use it to explain what they find.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Ben wants to find the mass of a small rock in grams. Which tool is the best to use?
choices: A ruler
A thermometer
A measuring jug
Kitchen scales
questions.explanation: Scales measure mass in grams. A ruler measures length and a jug measures liquid.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Ava measures a bean seedling each week. It is 3 cm in week 1, 6 cm in week 2 and 9 cm in week 3. If the pattern continues, how many centimetres tall will it be in week 4?
questions.explanation: The seedling grows 3 cm each week. In week 4 it will be 9 + 3 = 12 cm.
